```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# Chunks that use the network (a refgenie server and a public RefgetStore) run
# only when BIOCREFGETSTORE_RUN_REMOTE is set, like the package's live tests.
# Otherwise they are shown but not run. Chunks that need a local refgenie
# genome folder never run.
run_live <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("BIOCREFGETSTORE_RUN_REMOTE"))
```

Many Bioconductor tools take a reference genome as a
[BSgenome](https://bioconductor.org/packages/BSgenome/) object, which comes
from an installable data package such as `BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38`.
[Refgenie](https://refgenie.org) manages reference genomes and keeps the
sequences of each one in a
[RefgetStore](https://docs.refgenie.org/refget/refgetstore-explained/).
BiocRefgetStore reads a refgenie genome from that store, and `forgeBSgenome()`
builds a BSgenome data package from it. The package records the genome's
refgenie digest, so you can always tell which genome it holds.

You need BiocRefgetStore and gtars (see the
[Getting started](getting-started.html) vignette) and
[BSgenomeForge](https://bioconductor.org/packages/BSgenomeForge/):

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
BiocManager::install("BSgenomeForge")
```

## From a refgenie server

`RefgetGenome.from_refgenie()` opens a genome that a refgenie server lists, by
name. It asks the server (by default `https://api.refgenie.org`) for the
genome's digest and for the public RefgetStore that holds it, then opens the
genome from that store. This step downloads only metadata. To find a genome's
name, browse [refgenie.org](https://refgenie.org/genomes); this example uses
the yeast genome `R64-1-1`.

```{r open, eval = run_live}
library(BiocRefgetStore)
genome <- RefgetGenome.from_refgenie("R64-1-1")
genome
```

Store data is cached under `tools::R_user_dir("BiocRefgetStore", "cache")`, in
one folder per store. Pass `cache_path` to use another folder.

Now forge the package. Its name follows the BSgenome convention
`BSgenome.<organism>.<provider>.<build>`, and each part may hold only letters
and numbers, so `R64-1-1` becomes `R6411`. List the circular sequences in
`circ_seqs`; check `seqnames(genome)` for their names (`Mito` in this yeast
genome, `chrM` in hg38).

```{r forge, eval = run_live}
pkg <- forgeBSgenome(genome, "BSgenome.Scerevisiae.refgenie.R6411",
                     organism = "Saccharomyces cerevisiae",
                     circ_seqs = "Mito", dest = tempdir())
```

Install and load it like any other source package:

```{r install-forged, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(pkg, repos = NULL, type = "source")
library(BSgenome.Scerevisiae.refgenie.R6411)
```

```{r install-forged-live, include = FALSE, eval = run_live}
# The same as above, into a temporary library, so building this vignette does
# not change your R library.
forged_lib <- tempfile("forged_lib_")
dir.create(forged_lib)
install.packages(pkg, repos = NULL, type = "source", lib = forged_lib, quiet = TRUE)
library(BSgenome.Scerevisiae.refgenie.R6411, lib.loc = forged_lib)
```

The package exports a BSgenome object named after the second part of the
package name:

```{r bsgenome, eval = run_live}
Scerevisiae
getSeq(Scerevisiae, "Mito", 1, 60)
```

## From a local refgenie genome folder

Refgenie keeps the sequences of the genomes it manages in
`<genome_folder>/.refget_store`, and stores genome names there under the alias
namespace `"refgenie"`. The genome folder is `~/.refgenie/genomes` unless you
set `REFGENIE_GENOME_FOLDER` (see
[Configure refgenie](https://docs.refgenie.org/refgenie/configuration/)).

```{r local, eval = FALSE}
genome <- RefgetGenome.from_directory("~/.refgenie/genomes/.refget_store",
                                      namespace = "refgenie", alias = "R64-1-1")
pkg <- forgeBSgenome(genome, "BSgenome.Scerevisiae.refgenie.R6411",
                     organism = "Saccharomyces cerevisiae",
                     circ_seqs = "Mito", dest = tempdir())
```

This reads sequences from your disk. It works for a genome whose sequences
refgenie loaded into the store, such as one initialized from a FASTA file with
`refgenie genome init --fasta`. A genome registered from a server with
`refgenie genome init --server ... --no-build` has only its metadata (names,
lengths and digests) in the local store, so reading its sequences stops with
an error saying the bases could not be loaded. Open that genome with
`RefgetGenome.from_refgenie()` and the same name instead.

## How the package ties back to refgenie

Refgenie identifies each genome by a digest computed from its sequences: its
[GA4GH sequence collection](https://ga4gh.github.io/refget/seqcols/) digest.
`collection_digest()` returns it, and `forgeBSgenome()` records it as the
package's `genome` field:

```{r digest, eval = run_live}
collection_digest(genome)
GenomeInfoDb::genome(Scerevisiae)[[1]]
```

Loading the package back into a RefgetStore recomputes the digest from the
sequences themselves, and gives the same value:

```{r roundtrip, eval = run_live}
collection_digest(RefgetGenome.from_bsgenome(Scerevisiae))
```

So the `genome` field of any forged package leads back to its refgenie genome.
It is the digest that `refgenie genome list` shows, and the server describes
the genome at `https://api.refgenie.org/v4/genomes/<digest>`; for this yeast
genome, see
[refgenie.org/genomes/ia9g4Myony-xxLsSc7eQOC_NdClGgPGu](https://refgenie.org/genomes/ia9g4Myony-xxLsSc7eQOC_NdClGgPGu).

## Sizes and times

Opening a genome downloads only metadata (about 40 KB for yeast). Forging
downloads each sequence once and keeps it in the cache folder, writes the
sequences to temporary FASTA files, and packs them into the package's `.2bit`
file. Installing is a standard `R CMD INSTALL`.

| Genome | Sequences | Bases | Download | Open | Forge | Install |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yeast `R64-1-1`, measured | 17 | 12.2 Mbp | 3.1 MB | 2.5 s | 6.2 s | 12.7 s |
| Human `hg38`, estimated | 195 | 3.1 Gbp | 1.4 GB | | | |

The yeast numbers come from one run on one workstation with an empty cache.
The hg38 row is an estimate, not a measurement: its download is the total size
of its 195 sequence files in the public store, and its temporary FASTA files
need about 3.1 GB of disk while forging. Its times were not measured.
